cases.event: One autumn, riders at {E} reported that many of the fictional shared bikes felt slow and hard to pedal.
cases.q: What most likely made the shared bikes at {E} hard to pedal?
restate: Riders at {E} said the bikes felt slow and hard to pedal, and the question asks why.
Something made the shared bikes at {E} hard to pedal.
cases.answer: Dry, rusty chains most likely made the bikes at {E} hard to pedal, because a dry chain wastes much of the rider's effort.
cases.sum: the evidence points to the dry, rusty chains as the reason the bikes were hard to pedal.
cases.myth: The bikes at {E} were hard to pedal because the riders had grown too tall for them.
cases.mythClause: only the red bikes were hard to pedal
cases.altText: Some riders suggested that the tires on the bikes at {E} were not filled with enough air.
cases.patternQ: What pattern connects chain oiling and how the bikes at {E} felt?
cases.patternA: The bikes became hard to pedal after weeks without chain oiling and felt normal again once the chains were oiled, so the problem followed the chains.
cases.patternSum: how the bikes felt changed with the condition of their chains.

obs.text: A mechanic found that the chains on the slow bikes were dry and rusty.
exps: a dry, rusty chain drags against the gears and wastes the rider's effort

obs.text: After the mechanics oiled every chain, complaints at {E} dropped to almost zero within {n1} days.
exps: the problem went away once the chains were oiled, which is what would happen if the chains were the cause
fixing the chains fixed the bikes, so the two are linked
once the cause was removed, the effect faded
